title: सितारे क्यों झिलमिलाते हैं? विज्ञान में छुपा रहस्य
prompt: Create a 45‑60 second vertical explainer about why stars appear to twinkle while planets look steady. The hook must be a one‑breath question like “Ever wondered why stars sparkle but planets don’t?” Use stock footage of night skies, close‑ups of stars, planet imagery, and atmospheric visuals (clouds, wind). Explain the surprising angle: tiny temperature‑driven air currents bend starlight, causing rapid flicker; planets are closer and appear as discs, so the effect averages out. No charts or heavy jargon needed.

title: बिल्ली हमेशा पैर पर क्यों उतरती है? विज्ञान का रहस्य
prompt: Create a 45‑60 second vertical short that explains why cats can twist mid‑air and always land on their feet. Use stock footage of cats jumping, falling, and landing (including slow‑motion clips), plus any generic close‑up shots of a cat's spine or whiskers to illustrate the righting reflex. Keep the narration clear, wonder‑filled, and in Hindi, emphasizing the curiosity gap: why does this happen?

title: आइस्क्रीम खाने पर अचानक दिमाग में तेज़ दर्द क्यों होता है?
prompt: Create a 45‑60 second vertical explainer about why a sudden "brain freeze" (ice‑cream headache) happens when you eat something cold too quickly. Open with a one‑breath hook that asks viewers if they’ve ever felt that sharp pain in their head after a quick lick of ice‑cream. Explain the nerve‑signal mix‑up between the mouth and brain, using stock footage of ice‑cream, someone eating it fast, close‑up of a tongue, and visual metaphors of nerves flashing, plus a quick cut to a brain diagram (static image) to illustrate the pain signal. Keep language simple, no charts, no jargon.

title: ट्रेन के ब्रेक की चिल्लाहट क्यों सुनते हैं? विज्ञान का रहस्य
prompt: Create a 45‑60 second vertical explainer using only stock footage of trains, tracks, brake systems, and visualizations of vibrations. Narrate in Hindi, starting with a hook that makes viewers wonder why trains emit that loud, high‑pitched squeal when they brake. Explain the physics: friction between brake pads and wheels creates rapid vibration, the metal surfaces resonate, and the sound serves as a safety cue. Keep language simple, avoid technical jargon, and end with a quick recap.

title: टोस्ट हमेशा मक्खन वाली साइड नीचे क्यों गिरता है? | फ़िज़िक्स का रहस्य
prompt: Create a 45‑60 second vertical explainer about why a piece of toast almost always lands butter‑side down when it falls. Highlight the surprising physics: the offset center of mass, the typical drop height causing a half‑rotation, and the role of butter spreading. Open with the hook: “Ever wonder why your toast always lands butter‑side down?” Use only stock footage of toast being sliced, buttered, dropped, slow‑motion flip, kitchen surfaces, and a hand catching it.

title: सुनते ही गूज़बम्प क्यों बनते हैं? आपका शरीर डर से क्यों कांपता है!
prompt: Create a 45-60 second faceless explainer about the sudden goosebumps (piloerection) people get when they hear a scary sound. Start with the hook: "Why does your skin literally stand up when you hear a scary sound?" Use stock footage of people reacting to sudden loud/shriek sounds, close‑up shots of skin where goosebumps appear, animals (cats, dogs) with fur standing on end, and a quick montage of ancient humans in fur coats. Explain the surprising angle: it's a vestigial reflex from our hairy ancestors that made us look bigger and trapped warm air to keep us warm, now triggered by emotional arousal. Keep narration simple, no jargon, in Hindi.

title: सूर्योदय‑सूर्यास्त में आकाश लाल क्यों होता है? जानिए विज्ञान का राज
prompt: Create a 45‑60 second vertical explainer about why the sky turns red during sunrise and sunset. Open with a one‑breath hook that asks the viewer why the horizon glows crimson. Use only stock footage of dawn/dusk skies, sun rays, clouds, simple lab‑style light scattering demos, and close‑up of the sun’s edge. Script should explain in Hindi how longer atmospheric path scatters blue light, leaving red wavelengths, without needing diagrams or jargon.

title: फ्रीज़र में बोतल रखी तो क्यों फट जाती है? विज्ञान का रहस्य
prompt: Create a 45‑60 second vertical explainer using stock footage that shows a glass bottle being placed in a freezer, the ice forming inside, and the bottle shattering when removed. Open with a hook that asks why a simple bottle can explode in the freezer, then explain the physics of water expansion, pressure buildup, and glass strength in simple Hindi narration. Use clear, close‑up shots of the bottle, freezer door, and the break‑apart moment; no on‑screen text needed.

title: कुत्ते क्यों झुका रहे हैं सिर? विज्ञान से जानिए चुटीला कारण!
prompt: Create a 45-60 second vertical explainer using only stock footage and photos. Topic: why dogs tilt their heads when you talk. Surprising angle: it's not just cuteness, it's a clever adaptation to better locate sounds and interpret human facial cues. Hook to open with in one breath: "Ever wonder why dogs tilt their heads every time you speak?"

title: चार्ज पर फोन इस्तेमाल करने से बैटरी क्यों जल्दी ख़त्म हो जाती है? जानिए कारण
prompt: Create a 45‑60 second vertical explainer using only stock footage of smartphones, charging cables, batteries, heat visuals, and close‑ups of battery indicators. Topic: Why does a phone’s battery drain faster when you use it while it’s charging? The surprising angle: the hidden heat and voltage stress that actually harms the battery, not just the power draw. Opening hook (one breath): "क्या आपने कभी सोचा है कि चार्ज करते‑समय फोन इस्तेमाल करने से बैटरी जल्दी ख़त्म क्यों हो जाती है?" The narration should explain in simple Hindi the concepts of heat buildup, voltage spikes, and chemical stress, ending with a practical tip to avoid this.

title: हम्मिंगबर्ड हवा में क्यों रुकता है? जानिए प्रकृति का रहस्य
prompt: Create a 45‑60 second vertical video explaining why hummingbirds can hover in mid‑air. Emphasize the surprising fact that they achieve this by beating their wings in a figure‑8 pattern at around 80 beats per second, generating lift on both the upstroke and downstroke. Open with a single‑sentence hook that poses the curiosity gap: “Ever wonder how a hummingbird can stay perfectly still in the air?” Use only stock footage of hummingbirds, close‑ups of wing motion, flowers, and natural scenery – no presenters, no animations, no charts.

title: हवाई जहाज़ के पीछे सफ़ेद धुंध क्यों बनती है? रहस्य खुला!
prompt: Create a 45‑60 second vertical explainer about why airplanes leave white streaks (contrails) in the sky. Emphasize the surprising angle that these trails are actually ice crystals formed from water vapor in the hot engine exhaust mixing with the cold upper‑atmosphere, and that they can affect climate. Start with the hook: "क्या आपने कभी सोचा है कि हाई स्काई में हवाई जहाज़ के पीछे वो सफ़ेद धुंध क्यों बनती है?" Use only real stock footage: planes taking off/ cruising, close‑up of engine exhaust, high‑altitude clouds, time‑lapse sky, and simple on‑screen captions. No presenters, animations, or charts.

title: गर्मियों में सड़क पर जल जैसा दिखने वाला मिराज़ क्यों बनता है?
prompt: Create a 45‑60 second vertical explainer about why mirages appear on hot roads. Use the surprising angle that mirages are optical tricks caused by light refraction through layers of hot and cool air, not actual water. Open with a hook that makes the viewer picture a shimmering water patch on a scorching highway and wonder why it isn’t real. Gather stock footage of sun‑baked asphalt, heat waves, a car driving, close‑ups of light distortion, and a scientist or narrator (no presenter) explaining the refraction effect with simple narration.

title: उड़ान में कान पॉप क्यों करता है? फ़्लाइट का रहस्य
prompt: Create a 45‑60 second vertical explainer about why our ears pop during an airplane's ascent and descent. Start with the hook: "Your ear pops in a plane – why?" Explain the pressure difference between the cabin and the inner ear, the role of the eustachian tube in equalising pressure, and why the pop feels like a click. Use only stock footage and photographs: interior of a commercial aircraft, passengers looking uncomfortable, a close‑up of a pressure gauge, a clear stock image of the ear canal/eustachian tube, and shots of clouds/air at altitude. Narration should be in Hindi, simple everyday language, no charts or complex diagrams.

title: ऑक्टोपस का रंग बदलने का राज: एक झटके में अदृश्य क्यों?
prompt: Create a 45‑60 second faceless explainer using stock footage of octopuses, underwater scenes, close‑ups of skin patterns, and neural diagrams (as simple overlays). Focus on the surprising mechanism that lets an octopus change its color and texture in a split second – the hidden skin cells (chromatophores, iridophores, leucophores) and direct neural control. Open with the hook: "Ever wondered why an octopus can disappear in a blink?" Keep narration in Hindi, avoid technical jargon, and end with a quick “next time you see one, notice the instant color flash!”

title: शहद की छत्ती क्यों बनती है षट्कोणीय? विज्ञान का आश्चर्य

Use only stock footage of bees, honeycombs, wax, and simple shape overlays—no diagrams or on‑screen text. Open with the hook sentence provided below.

title: गूदड़ क्यों होते हैं? ठंड और भावनाओं का आश्चर्यजनक कारण
prompt: Create a 45‑60 second vertical explainer that reveals why humans get goosebumps (रूद/गूदड़) when they feel cold or experience strong emotions. Open with a one‑breath hook: "Ever wondered why your skin prickles when you hear a moving song or a scary story?" Use only real stock footage: close‑up of skin with goosebumps, people shivering, emotional moments, animals (cats, birds) raising fur, and a quick cut to an ancient human silhouette to hint at the survival instinct. No charts or animations needed.

title: नीचे हुआ चाँद क्यों लगता है बड़ा? सच्चा कारण बताएं

title: रगड़ते ही गुब्बारा छत से चिपक जाता है? कारण जानिए!
prompt: Create a 45‑60 second vertical video explaining why a simple latex balloon, when rubbed against hair or a sweater, suddenly sticks to the ceiling. Open with a single‑breath hook that asks the viewer why the balloon clings, creating a curiosity gap they must close.

title: कार की खिड़की अंदर से धुंध क्यों बनती है? रहस्य खुला!
prompt: Create a 45‑60 second vertical video explaining why a car’s windshield fogs up from the inside. Use the curiosity gap: viewers wonder why the glass suddenly becomes hazy when they breathe inside a cold car. The surprising angle is that warm, moist breath meets the cold glass, causing condensation – a simple physics trick we all experience daily. Open with a single‑breath hook that poses the question directly. Use only stock footage: close‑ups of a fogged windshield, breath vapor, cold weather exterior, driver adjusting defroster, and a quick demo of wiping the glass. No charts, no presenter, no animation.

title: बिजली की शाखा जैसी चमक का रहस्य खुलासा! क्यों बनती है ये?
prompt: Create a 45‑60 second vertical explainer using only stock footage and photos. Topic: the branching, tree‑like shape of lightning bolts. Surprising angle: reveal that the jagged branches are formed by a step‑wise discharge called the "stepped leader" and the way ionized air creates multiple paths, not random chance. Hook (first sentence): "क्या आपने कभी सोचा है कि बिजली की चमक शाखा‑जैसी क्यों दिखती है?" Gather footage of storm clouds, close‑up lightning, slow‑motion lab high‑voltage discharge, and animated (but stock‑style) diagrams of ionized paths. No presenter, no animation beyond stock clips. Keep narration in Hindi, simple everyday language.

title: प्याज़ काटते ही आँसू क्यों आते हैं? विज्ञान का रहस्य

Begin with a one‑sentence hook that asks the viewer why chopping a simple vegetable can turn your eyes into a waterfall.

title: फ़ोन तकिये पर चार्ज करने से ज़्यादा गरम क्यों हो जाता है? | विज्ञान का राज
prompt: Create a 45‑60 second vertical explainer about why a smartphone gets noticeably hotter when it is charged on a soft surface like a pillow or blanket. title: एक हाई नोट से काँच क्यों टूट जाता है? साउंड रेज़ोनेंस का रहस्य

Explain the concept of acoustic resonance in simple Hindi without technical jargon. Use engaging background music and clear narration.

title: बारिश के बाद की जादुई ख़ुशबू क्यों आती है? पटरिचोर का रहस्य
prompt: Create a 45‑60 second vertical explainer video using only real stock footage and photographs (no presenter, no animation) about why the ground emits a distinct scent after rain. title: जब गाना बजता है तो रेंगते रेशे क्यों बनते हैं? विज्ञान का सच
